Opprobrium

uh-PROH-bree-um · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Opprobrium is harsh public criticism or disgrace resulting from shameful conduct.

The company faced widespread opprobrium after the safety cover-up came to light.

Worked Example

The senator resigned amid public opprobrium after the scandal broke on every news channel.

Harsh, widespread public disgrace, not just private disappointment, is exactly what opprobrium describes.

How Opprobrium Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

disgrace

disgrace: loss of reputation from shameful conduct

condemnation

condemnation: strong public disapproval

Antonyms

acclaim

acclaim: enthusiastic public approval

honor

honor: public respect and esteem

How Strong Is It? — criticism → opprobrium → infamy

criticism vs. opprobrium

criticism vs. opprobrium: Criticism can be private or public, mild or strong; opprobrium is specifically harsh, public disgrace.

infamy vs. opprobrium

infamy vs. opprobrium: Infamy goes even further than opprobrium, implying the shameful reputation becomes lasting and widely known.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Opprobrium comes from Latin ob- ('against') + probrum ('a shameful, disgraceful act') -- literally something shameful thrown against a person's reputation.

Use the root in a new word: opprobrious

Use the root in a new word: opprobrious: The related adjective opprobrious ('expressing scornful reproach') comes from exactly the same Latin root.

Word Building

Word Choice

Opprobrium is formal and public in scale -- reserve it for widespread, reputation-damaging disgrace, not personal embarrassment.
